blocks.text: The nervous system carries out fast nervous coordination, while the endocrine system controls long-term processes such as growth, metabolism and reproduction. It does this by sending chemical instructions, hormones, to target parts of the body; this is chemical coordination.

blocks.title: Hormone
blocks.text: A hormone is a regulatory chemical secreted into the blood or tissue fluid by an endocrine gland. The blood carries it to every cell, but it acts only on its specific target cells, which respond in a specific way; so hormones are called chemical messengers or signalling molecules.

blocks.title: Exocrine and endocrine glands
blocks.text: Glands are tissues that produce and release secretions. Exocrine glands pour their secretions into ducts; endocrine glands are ductless and release their secretions, hormones, straight into the blood or tissue fluid.

blocks.title: The first hormone
blocks.text: In 1902 Bayliss and Starling found that when acidic gastric juice enters the small intestine, a substance they called secretin is released into the blood; it reaches the pancreas and makes it secrete pancreatic juice.

blocks.prompt: Why is a hormone called a chemical messenger?
blocks.explanation: It is a chemical released into the blood that carries a message from its gland to distant target cells, which respond to it in a specific way.

items: Endocrine system: long-term control (growth, metabolism, reproduction) by hormones; hormones reach all cells but act only on target cells.
